questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This surgical illustration compares normal mitral valve anatomy with a ring sutured around the mitral annulus (cross-sectional and inferior cut-away views). What is the primary purpose of the device being placed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To reduce annular dilation and restore leaflet coaptation in mitral regurgitation

choices.label: B
choices.text: To occlude the left atrial appendage and prevent emboli

choices.label: C
choices.text: To replace the entire valve with a mechanical prosthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: To pace the atrium and control atrial fibrillation

choices.label: E
choices.text: To widen a fused, stenotic mitral orifice

explanation.summary: The device is an annuloplasty ring. It is sewn around a dilated mitral annulus to shrink and reshape it, allowing the native leaflets to coapt again and thereby correcting regurgitation while preserving the patient's own valve.
explanation.whyCorrect: The device is an annuloplasty ring. It is sewn around a dilated mitral annulus to shrink and reshape it, allowing the native leaflets to coapt again and thereby correcting regurgitation while preserving the patient's own valve.

questions.stem: This diagram labels the components of a heart valve, including the anterior annulus, anterior leaflet, chordae tendineae, and papillary muscles. Which valve's apparatus is depicted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aortic valve

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tricuspid valve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eustachian valve

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pulmonary valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mitral valve

explanation.summary: The two leaflets suspended by chordae tendineae from papillary muscles, with an anterior and posterior leaflet arrangement, are characteristic of the mitral (bicuspid) valve between the left atrium and left ventricle.
explanation.whyCorrect: The two leaflets suspended by chordae tendineae from papillary muscles, with an anterior and posterior leaflet arrangement, are characteristic of the mitral (bicuspid) valve between the left atrium and left ventricle.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This histologic section of a mitral leaflet shows the fibrosa, an irregularly thickened spongiosa layer, and the atrialis. Which valvular disorder does this expanded, disorganized spongiosa indicate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amyloid infiltration of the valve stroma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rheumatic valvulitis with Aschoff bodies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Myxomatous degeneration causing mitral valve prolapse

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infective endocarditis with fibrin-platelet vegetations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Calcific degeneration with dystrophic calcification

explanation.summary: Accumulation of proteoglycan-rich ground substance expands the spongiosa and fragments the fibrosa, weakening the leaflet. This myxomatous (myxoid) degeneration produces the redundant, floppy leaflets of mitral valve prolapse.
explanation.whyCorrect: Accumulation of proteoglycan-rich ground substance expands the spongiosa and fragments the fibrosa, weakening the leaflet. This myxomatous (myxoid) degeneration produces the redundant, floppy leaflets of mitral valve prolapse.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This parasternal long-axis echocardiogram shows systolic billowing of the mitral leaflets more than 2 mm above the annular plane (red line). What auscultatory finding is classically associated with this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pericardial friction rub

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fixed splitting of S2

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mid-systolic click

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opening snap

choices.label: E
choices.text: S3 gallop

explanation.summary: Displacement of redundant myxomatous leaflets above the annulus defines mitral valve prolapse, which produces a mid-systolic click (often followed by a late systolic murmur if regurgitation is present).
explanation.whyCorrect: Displacement of redundant myxomatous leaflets above the annulus defines mitral valve prolapse, which produces a mid-systolic click (often followed by a late systolic murmur if regurgitation is present).

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This opened heart shows a mitral valve with fibrotic, thickened, fused leaflets narrowing the orifice. What auscultatory finding is most expected from this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Opening snap followed by a diastolic rumble

choices.label: B
choices.text: Early diastolic decrescendo murmur

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continuous machine-like murmur

choices.label: D
choices.text: Crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur

choices.label: E
choices.text: Holosystolic murmur at the apex

explanation.summary: Leaflet fibrosis, thickening, and commissural fusion produce mitral stenosis, which classically causes an opening snap and a low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble; a holosystolic murmur would indicate regurgitation instead.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leaflet fibrosis, thickening, and commissural fusion produce mitral stenosis, which classically causes an opening snap and a low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble; a holosystolic murmur would indicate regurgitation instead.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This explanted valve shows thickened leaflets with fusion at the commissures (arrows). What is the most common underlying etiology worldwide for this valvular deformity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infective endocarditis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Congenital bicuspid malformation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rheumatic heart disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Myxomatous degeneration

choices.label: E
choices.text: Carcinoid heart disease

explanation.summary: Commissural fusion with leaflet and chordal thickening producing a fish-mouth orifice is the hallmark of chronic rheumatic valvulitis, the leading cause of mitral stenosis worldwide.
explanation.whyCorrect: Commissural fusion with leaflet and chordal thickening producing a fish-mouth orifice is the hallmark of chronic rheumatic valvulitis, the leading cause of mitral stenosis worldwide.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: These two illustrations show a chorda tendinea rupture and a papillary muscle rupture affecting the mitral apparatus. What clinical presentation do these mechanisms most characteristically cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Slowly progressive tricuspid regurgitation with peripheral edema

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gradual aortic regurgitation with a wide pulse pressure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acute severe mitral regurgitation with sudden pulmonary edema

choices.label: D
choices.text: Asymptomatic mid-systolic click without hemodynamic effect

choices.label: E
choices.text: Chronic compensated mitral stenosis with atrial enlargement

explanation.summary: Rupture of a chorda or papillary muscle (classically a few days after inferior MI) abruptly deprives a leaflet of support, causing acute severe mitral regurgitation. Because the atrium and pulmonary vasculature have no time to adapt, patients present with sudden flash pulmonary edema and hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rupture of a chorda or papillary muscle (classically a few days after inferior MI) abruptly deprives a leaflet of support, causing acute severe mitral regurgitation. Because the atrium and pulmonary vasculature have no time to adapt, patients present with sudden flash pulmonary edema and hypotension.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This cardiac diagram depicts asymmetric septal thickening with a high-velocity outflow jet and a posteriorly directed mitral regurgitant jet. What mechanism directly causes the mitral regurgitation shown?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ruptured chordae tendineae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Annular calcification

choices.label: C
choices.text: Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve leaflet

choices.label: D
choices.text: Papillary muscle infarction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Leaflet vegetation from endocarditis

explanation.summary: In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the hypertrophied septum accelerates outflow, drawing the anterior mitral leaflet toward the septum (systolic anterior motion), which obstructs outflow and creates a posteriorly directed regurgitant jet.
explanation.whyCorrect: In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the hypertrophied septum accelerates outflow, drawing the anterior mitral leaflet toward the septum (systolic anterior motion), which obstructs outflow and creates a posteriorly directed regurgitant jet.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This left ventricular pressure-volume loop compares the normal loop with that of chronic mitral regurgitation. What key hemodynamic change does the regurgitant loop demonstrate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A prolonged isovolumetric relaxation phase with normal volumes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased end-diastolic volume with a larger total stroke volume and loss of isovolumetric contraction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated afterload with a tall, narrow loop

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced end-diastolic volume with a narrow stroke volume

choices.label: E
choices.text: Decreased preload with reduced ejection

explanation.summary: In chronic MR the incompetent valve allows systolic backflow, so there is no true isovolumetric contraction; volume overload raises LVEDV and total (forward plus regurgitant) stroke volume, widening and right-shifting the loop.
explanation.whyCorrect: In chronic MR the incompetent valve allows systolic backflow, so there is no true isovolumetric contraction; volume overload raises LVEDV and total (forward plus regurgitant) stroke volume, widening and right-shifting the loop.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: These two phonocardiogram tracings contrast murmurs occurring between S1 and S2. What feature distinguishes the lower (mitral regurgitation) tracing from the upper (aortic stenosis) tracing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A uniform holosystolic (plateau) murmur rather than a crescendo-decrescendo shape

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a mid-diastolic rumble after an opening snap

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a continuous murmur spanning S2

choices.label: D
choices.text: It occurs entirely in diastole

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is an early diastolic decrescendo murmur

explanation.summary: Mitral regurgitation produces a uniform-intensity holosystolic murmur because the pressure gradient between LV and LA is constant throughout systole, whereas aortic stenosis produces a crescendo-decrescendo ejection murmur that tapers before S2.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mitral regurgitation produces a uniform-intensity holosystolic murmur because the pressure gradient between LV and LA is constant throughout systole, whereas aortic stenosis produces a crescendo-decrescendo ejection murmur that tapers before S2.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This phonocardiogram diagram shows the midsystolic click and late systolic murmur of mitral valve prolapse and how they shift after sudden standing versus sudden squatting. What accounts for the click and murmur occurring EARLIER after sudden standing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased venous return reduces LV volume, so the prolapse and click occur earlier in systole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated left atrial pressure prevents the leaflets from prolapsing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bradycardia lengthens diastole and shifts the murmur toward S1

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased LV filling stretches the chordae and abolishes the click

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased afterload delays leaflet coaptation, moving the click later

explanation.summary: Standing decreases preload and LV end-diastolic volume; the smaller ventricle allows the redundant leaflet to prolapse sooner, moving the click and murmur closer to S1. Squatting increases preload and afterload, enlarging the LV and delaying the click toward S2.
explanation.whyCorrect: Standing decreases preload and LV end-diastolic volume; the smaller ventricle allows the redundant leaflet to prolapse sooner, moving the click and murmur closer to S1. Squatting increases preload and afterload, enlarging the LV and delaying the click toward S2.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal mitral valve with a regurgitant one during ventricular systole. What is the direct hemodynamic consequence of the abnormality shown on the right?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood regurgitates from the aorta back into the left ventricle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood is obstructed as it enters the left ventricle during diastole

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blood flows backward from the left ventricle into the left atrium during systole

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blood pools in the pulmonary veins without entering the atrium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Blood shunts from the left atrium to the right atrium

explanation.summary: When the mitral leaflets fail to coapt during systole, a portion of the LV stroke volume is ejected retrograde into the left atrium instead of forward into the aorta, producing the holosystolic murmur and volume overload of mitral regurgitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: When the mitral leaflets fail to coapt during systole, a portion of the LV stroke volume is ejected retrograde into the left atrium instead of forward into the aorta, producing the holosystolic murmur and volume overload of mitral regurgitation.

questions.topicName: Mitral Regurgitation and Mitral Valve Prolapse
questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal left ventricle with one in which the papillary muscle is displaced, the leaflets are tethered, and closure is restricted. What type of mitral regurgitation does this mechanism represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Primary regurgitation from a torn, flail leaflet

choices.label: B
choices.text: Functional (secondary) regurgitation from LV remodeling that tethers structurally normal leaflets

choices.label: C
choices.text: Regurgitation from infective vegetations destroying the cusp

choices.label: D
choices.text: Congenital regurgitation from a cleft anterior leaflet

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rheumatic regurgitation from commissural fusion and thickening

explanation.summary: When ventricular dilation displaces the papillary muscles outward, the chordae tether otherwise normal leaflets and prevent full closure. This is functional (secondary) mitral regurgitation, driven by ventricular geometry rather than intrinsic valve disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: When ventricular dilation displaces the papillary muscles outward, the chordae tether otherwise normal leaflets and prevent full closure. This is functional (secondary) mitral regurgitation, driven by ventricular geometry rather than intrinsic valve disease.
